profile.summary: S2F (Sequence-Structure Fitness model) predicts how amino acid substitutions change protein fitness without training on any fitness data. It feeds per-residue outputs of the ESM-2-650M protein language model into a graph network built over the protein backbone structure. The input is a wild-type sequence, its predicted structure (AlphaFold2 in the paper) and the substitutions to score; the output is one score per mutant.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: Overview; Paper: Abstract, section 1, section 4.1

summary_quotes.text: We begin with a Sequence-Structure Fitness Model (S2F) by combining a protein language model with a structure-based encoder.
S2F utilizes the output of the protein language model as node features
We use AlphaFold2 to predict the wild-type structures.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: S2F builds a radius graph over alpha carbons (edges under 10 Å) and runs Geometric Vector Perceptron (GVP) message passing, starting from ESM-2-650M embeddings as node features. The paper gives 5 GVP layers with 100 scalar and 16 vector hidden features; the released s2f.yaml config sets node_h_dim to [256, 16]. Pre-training predicts masked residue types on 30,948 CATH v4.3.0 structures with ESM-2-650M frozen, so only the GVP layers are trained. At inference, mutation sites are masked; for residues with AlphaFold2 pLDDT below 70 the ESM-2-650M score is used instead.

sections.body: The repository and Zenodo record 14257708 (published 2024-12-02) provide two checkpoints: s2f.pth (2,684,305,563 bytes) and s3f.pth (2,844,210,889 bytes). S2F uses s2f.pth. Both also need the ESM-2-650M weights (esm2_t33_650M_UR50D.pt). A result should name the checkpoint file, the commit of the code and the structures used.

sections.title: What distinguishes S2F
sections.body: S2F is the sequence and structure model without the surface encoder of S3F and without the EVE ensemble of S2F-MSA. It needs no surface graphs and no alignment.

quotes.text: which enhances S2F by adding a protein surface encoder that represents surfaces as point clouds and facilitates message passing between neighboring points.
ensembling them with EVE predictions through the summation of their z-scores, resulting in two variants named S2F-MSA and S3F-MSA.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: ESM-2-650M embeddings as node features for 5 GVP message-passing layers over a 10 Å alpha-carbon radius graph. Hidden sizes differ between paper (100 scalar, 16 vector) and released config ([256, 16]).

quotes.text: Practically, we utilize L = 5 layers of GVP, with d′ = 16 vector and d = 100 scalar hidden representations.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: One fitness score per mutant. The evaluation script writes output files to ~/scratch/proteingym_output, set by output_dir in the config.

quotes.text: The output files can be found at `~/scratch/proteingym_output`, which is specified by the `output_dir` argument in the `*.yaml`.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 6M trainable parameters for S2F, as listed in the paper's Table 1. ESM-2-650M is frozen inside the model and is not counted as trainable.

quotes.text: During pre-training, the weights of the ESM2-650M model are frozen, and only the GVP layers for structure and surface graphs are trainable.

facts.value: A non-redundant subset of CATH v4.3.0: 30,948 experimental structures with under 40% sequence identity. ESM-2-650M weights are reused, not retrained.

quotes.text: Our models are pre-trained on a non-redundant subset of CATH v4.3.0 dataset (CC BY 4.0 license) [30],

limitations.text: Assumes the backbone does not change on mutation and ignores side chains; for low-confidence residues (pLDDT below 70) it falls back to ESM-2-650M scores.

run_guide.summary: Install the S3F code at a pinned commit, download ProteinGym data, the ESM-2-650M weights and the S2F checkpoint, and score all ProteinGym substitution assays.
prerequisites: Python 3.7 or 3.8 and PyTorch 1.8.0 with CUDA 11.1, as the README states.
One GPU; evaluation is single-GPU only and the README reports about 20 hours for all 217 assays on one A100.
Code is MIT; the Zenodo checkpoint record is CC BY 4.0.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/DeepGraphLearning/S3F.git
cd S3F
git checkout --detach 2efab6adfb27b8b36f99059a355125ce181fdaf0
steps.explanation: The README gives no clone command; these lines fetch the repository at the commit this page was written from.

quotes.text: This is the official codebase of the paper

steps.title: Install dependencies (pip route)
steps.shell:
pip install torch==1.8.0+cu111 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/lts/1.8/torch_lts.html
pip install torchdrug
pip install easydict pyyaml
steps.explanation: The README's pip installation. It also gives a conda alternative.

quotes.text: pip install torch==1.8.0+cu111 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/lts/1.8/torch_lts.html

steps.title: Download ProteinGym data
steps.shell:
wget https://marks.hms.harvard.edu/proteingym/DMS_ProteinGym_substitutions.zip -O ./dataset
unzip DMS_ProteinGym_substitutions.zip -d ./dataset/DMS_ProteinGym_substitutions
wget https://marks.hms.harvard.edu/proteingym/ProteinGym_AF2_structures.zip -O ./dataset
unzip ProteinGym_AF2_structures.zip -d ./dataset/ProteinGym_AF2_structures
steps.explanation: Copied as the README prints it. As written, -O ./dataset saves each zip to a file named dataset while unzip expects the zip in the current folder, so the download target may need adjusting.

quotes.text: wget https://marks.hms.harvard.edu/proteingym/DMS_ProteinGym_substitutions.zip -O ./dataset
unzip ProteinGym_AF2_structures.zip -d ./dataset/ProteinGym_AF2_structures

steps.title: Download the ESM-2-650M weights
steps.explanation: The model is built on ESM-2-650M. The path must match task.model.sequence_model.path in the config.

path: ~/scratch/protein-model-weights/esm-model-weights/

steps.title: Download the S2F checkpoint
steps.explanation: The README links the Zenodo record without a file URL; this address is the s2f.pth download link in the Zenodo record metadata, and -O names the file.

quotes.text: https://zenodo.org/api/records/14257708/files/s2f.pth/content
You can download these checkpoints from [link](https://zenodo.org/records/14257708)

steps.title: Run S2F on ProteinGym
steps.explanation: The README command with <path_to_ckpt> replaced by the downloaded file. To score a subset of assays, the config has an id_list option.

quotes.text: python script/evaluate.py -c config/evaluate/s2f.yaml --datadir ./dataset/DMS_ProteinGym_substitutions --structdir ./dataset/ProteinGym_AF2_structures --ckpt <path_to_ckpt>
# id_list:      # If you only want to evaluate a subset of assays

outputs: Score files in ~/scratch/proteingym_output, the output_dir set in the config.
